newsitem.title: USA: Role of FBI bosses reviewed in Olympic bomb probe.
newsitem.headline: Role of FBI bosses reviewed in Olympic bomb probe.

text.p: FBI investigators reviewing the interrogation of former Olympics security guard Richard Jewell are looking at the role played by top FBI supervisors, the Washington Post reported in Sunday editions.

Jewell has been cleared as a suspect in the Olympics bombing. FBI Director Louis Freeh said last month his agency was conducting an inquiry into Jewell's interrogation and the "propriety" of the manner in which FBI agents questioned him.

The inquiry into whether Jewell's constitutional rights were violated encompasses senior headquarters staff amid mounting indications that the handling of Jewell was closely supervised from Washington, the Post said, quoting senior federal officials.

The officials told the paper investigators were looking closely at a conference call that linked FBI headquarters, the Atlanta FBI office and the Justice Department on the afternoon of July 30, when Jewell was with FBI agents in Atlanta.
FBI Director Louis Freeh took part in the conference call with the Atlanta agents, the Post reported.

During the call Freeh and Justice Department officials asked the agents to be certain Jewell was properly advised of his constitutional rights, although no explanation was offered of the circumstances for the request, the newspaper reported.

On July 30, after he had been named in news accounts as a possible suspect, two FBI agents went to Jewell's apartment and asked him to come to the FBI's office in Atlanta to help make a training film on how to question a witness.

During the videotaped session, one FBI agent told Jewell, a former security guard, that he wanted the film to be realistic and asked him to sign a waiver of his constitutional rights to remain silent and to have a lawyer present.

As Jewell was handed the waiver form he became concerned and asked to call a lawyer. His attorneys have said the FBI used the training film as a ruse in an attempt to get a videotaped statement that Jewell had waived his rights.
